problem: The chapter says the 60° and 150° landmarks appear in the delta branch quantities. With one thyristor pair in series with each delta branch, each branch is just a single-phase controller fed by the line-to-line voltage. Its conduction is continuous only up to α = 90°, and its RMS branch voltage reaches zero at α = 180°, not 150°.
fix: Replace with: "In the delta, each branch pair sees the line-to-line voltage and behaves as a single-phase controller: conduction stays continuous up to α = 90°, and the branch output falls to zero at α = 180°. The 60° and 150° landmarks belong to the three-wire star, not to the delta."

problem: It says a soft starter "raises the firing angle slowly so the motor voltage rises". Raising α lowers the output voltage, so this reverses the action of a soft starter.
fix: A soft starter starts with a large firing angle (near 180°) and reduces it slowly toward 0°, so the motor voltage ramps up from a small value without a large inrush current.

problem: The answer says the currents contain "triplen components that cannot return in the neutral". In a three-wire star the three load currents sum to zero at every instant, so the zero-sequence (triplen) current component is identically zero and cannot appear in the currents at all. This also contradicts Section 3, which says triplens need a neutral or delta path.
fix: The load is unbalanced. The floating star point shifts, so the three phase voltages are no longer the supply phase voltages and contain a zero-sequence (triplen) component. The line currents still sum to zero, so they can carry no zero-sequence current; only their DC and 5th, 7th, 11th … components change.

problem: The sentence "The supply phase voltage is:" introduces a formula for the output (load) phase voltage V_o,ph, not for the supply voltage.
fix: Write: "For 0 ≤ α ≤ 60°, the RMS load phase voltage is:"

problem: "Changing the firing angle of one phase therefore changes the voltages of the other two" is true only for the three-wire star. In a delta with an ideal source the branch voltages are the supply line voltages and do not shift when another branch's firing angle changes.
fix: Restrict the sentence: "In a three-wire star, changing the firing angle of one phase changes the voltages of the other two." Keep the delta out of that claim.

problem: "The zero point is α = 150° because no return path remains for a conducting pair" is vague and can be read as saying the return path disappears only at 150°, when in fact there is never a neutral in this circuit.
fix: "The zero point is α = 150° because a firing pulse at that instant comes after the relevant line-to-line voltage has already reversed, so no pair of devices can be turned on and no current can start."

problem: "Phase control produces odd harmonics: 5th, 7th, 11th and so on" mixes the single-phase picture (all odd orders) with the balanced three-phase picture, and leaves a student wondering where the 3rd went before triplens are discussed.
fix: Say: "With symmetrical firing in a balanced three-phase load, the line currents contain harmonics of order 6k ± 1: 5th, 7th, 11th, 13th and so on. Triplen orders (3rd, 9th, 15th) are the zero-sequence family, discussed next."
